chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, that

A woman from the progeny of al-Mukhtar swore an oath against her sister, or a relative of hers. She said: 'Come closer, so-and-so, and eat with me.' She replied: 'No.' So she swore and imposed upon herself: the walking to the House of God, and freeing all her slaves, and that neither herself nor the other would ever be shaded under the same roof, nor eat together at a table, ever. Then the other woman said the same.

So Umar ibn Hanzala brought both their statements to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: 'I am the arbiter in this matter. Tell her: let her eat, and let both of them be shaded under the same roof, and she need not walk (to the Kaaba), nor free (slaves), and let her fear God, her Lord, and not return to such things, for this is from the footsteps of Satan.'

key_terms.الْمَشْيَ إِلَى بَيْتِ اللَّهِ: walking to the House of God — a vow to make the hajj pilgrimage on foot as an act of penance
key_terms.خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ: footsteps of Satan — a Quranic phrase (2:168, 2:208) denoting actions inspired by the devil
key_terms.خِوَان: dining cloth or table — the surface upon which shared meals are spread
key_terms.عِتْق: emancipation — the freeing of one's slaves, used here as a vow penalty

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about oaths involving walking to the Kaaba and freeing slaves taken in anger?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) nullified a mutually retaliatory oath in which two women — one from the family of al-Mukhtar — imposed upon themselves extreme religious penalties (pilgrimage by foot, emancipation of slaves, permanent separation) out of anger. The Imam ruled that none of the oaths required fulfillment and admonished them, warning that such behavior is inspired by Satan. This hadith reflects the Imami jurisprudential principle that oaths taken in anger or in direct contradiction to social obligation are not binding, and that the Imam's authority as arbiter supersedes such hasty vows.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

‘A woman from the progeny of Al-Mukhtar swore an oath upon her sister or a relative of hers, so she said, ‘Come closer and eat with me’. So she said, ‘No’. So she swore and made it upon herself the walking to the House of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and free what she owned (slaves), and she would never shade herself and her under the roof of one house, nor eat with her upon a table, ever’. So the other one said similar to that.

So Umar Bin Hazala carried both their speeches to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> shall judge regarding that. Say to her, ‘Let her eat, and let her be shaded, and her under the roof of one house, and neither to walk (to the Kaaba), nor free a slave, and let her fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> her Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and not to exceed to that, for this is from the footsteps of the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following:

“A woman of the family of al-Mukhtar took an oath against her sister or a relative. She asked her to join her for food but she refused. She then took an oath and made it upon her-self to walk to the house of Allah, free a slave and never to live under one roof with her or eat with her on one table, and the other one did the same thing.

‘Umar ibn Hanzalah took this question before abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, and he (the Imam) said, ‘I can judge this case. She must eat, live under one roof with her, must not walk or set free a slave. She must have fear of Allah, her Lord, and must not transgress in such issues; it is of temptations of Satan.’”
